description: A single TypeScript Temporal workflow (order processing) deliberately riddled with anti-patterns in retry policies, timeouts, determinism, history management, and error handling. Intended as a teaching/demo artifact of what NOT to do. Connects to Temporal Cloud via namespace, endpoint, and API key or mTLS from environment variables.
rules: Every anti-pattern must be marked with a comment of the form // BAD IDEA: <short explanation of why it is bad>
Each story is implemented independently and must leave the project compiling with npm run build
Do not fix or soften any anti-pattern, even if it looks like a mistake
README must not contain a project-structure or file-tree section
Do not use Math.random or Date.now to demonstrate non-determinism; the TypeScript workflow sandbox makes them deterministic

userStories.title: Scaffold TypeScript Temporal project for Temporal Cloud
userStories.description: Create package.json, tsconfig, and dependencies for @temporalio/client, worker, workflow, and activity. Add a config module that reads namespace, address, and API key from environment variables to connect to Temporal Cloud.
acceptanceCriteria: npm install and npm run build succeed
Config reads TEMPORAL_ADDRESS, TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE, and TEMPORAL_API_KEY from env
No local dev server or self-hosted configuration is included

userStories.title: Create worker, client starter, and empty OrderWorkflow
userStories.description: Add a worker entrypoint, a client script that starts OrderWorkflow, and a skeleton workflow that calls placeholder activities: validateOrder, chargeCard, reserveInventory, shipOrder.
acceptanceCriteria: Worker starts and polls a task queue named cursed-orders
Starter script starts the workflow with a sample order
Builds cleanly

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: start-to-close timeout shorter than activity duration
userStories.description: Make shipOrder sleep about 10 seconds but configure startToCloseTimeout at 2 seconds so it always times out before completing.
acceptanceCriteria: shipOrder deliberately takes longer than its startToCloseTimeout
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: unlimited retries with no backoff
userStories.description: Set shipOrder retry policy to maximumAttempts 0 (unlimited), backoffCoefficient 1, and initialInterval of 100ms so it hammers forever.
acceptanceCriteria: Retry policy has unlimited attempts, coefficient 1, tiny initial interval
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: schedule-to-close shorter than start-to-close
userStories.description: On reserveInventory, set scheduleToCloseTimeout below startToCloseTimeout so retries can never fit in the window.
acceptanceCriteria: scheduleToCloseTimeout is smaller than startToCloseTimeout
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: tight heartbeat timeout on a non-heartbeating long activity
userStories.description: Add a long-running activity generateInvoicePdf that runs about 30 seconds, set heartbeatTimeout to 3 seconds, and never call heartbeat.
acceptanceCriteria: Activity never heartbeats
heartbeatTimeout is far shorter than runtime
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: non-determinism via mutable module-level state
userStories.description: Declare a module-level counter outside the workflow function and increment it on each workflow task. Use its value to decide whether to call an extra activity (for example, notifyWarehouse) before chargeCard, so the command sequence differs between original execution and replay. Do NOT use Math.random or Date.now, because the TypeScript workflow sandbox makes those deterministic.
acceptanceCriteria: Module-level mutable state influences which commands the workflow issues
Math.random and Date.now are not used for this story

A replay test using the SDK's Worker.runReplayHistory (or runReplayHistories) against a captured history confirms a non-determinism error is actually produced; if it is not, adjust the approach until it is
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment explaining the replay failure

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: network and environment access inside workflow code
userStories.description: Attempt a fetch call and read process.env inside workflow code to branch behavior. Keep the code present even if the sandbox rejects it, and document the failure mode in the comment.
acceptanceCriteria: Workflow code contains a fetch and a process.env branch
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: huge payload passed between activities
userStories.description: Have an activity return a multi-megabyte base64 blob (a fake product catalog) and pass it into the next activity as an argument.
acceptanceCriteria: Payload is large enough to approach Temporal payload limits
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: unbounded history with no continue-as-new
userStories.description: Add an order-status polling loop that runs forever, sleeping briefly and calling an activity each iteration, never calling continueAsNew.
acceptanceCriteria: Loop has no exit condition or continueAsNew
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: massive unthrottled child workflow fan-out
userStories.description: Add a notifyCustomers step that starts 10,000 child workflows at once via Promise.all with no batching.
acceptanceCriteria: 10,000 children started in one Promise.all
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: everything is retryable, including validation errors
userStories.description: Make validateOrder throw plain Errors for permanently invalid input, with an empty nonRetryableErrorTypes list, so it retries forever on bad data.
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid order throws a retryable error
No non-retryable error types configured

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: swallowed errors in a catch block
userStories.description: Wrap the inventory step in try/catch that ignores the error and continues as if it succeeded.
acceptanceCriteria: Catch block swallows the error with no logging or rethrow
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: non-idempotent chargeCard with no idempotency key
userStories.description: Implement chargeCard so each execution creates a new charge in an in-memory ledger, with no idempotency key, combined with aggressive retries and timeouts so duplicate charges are likely.
acceptanceCriteria: No idempotency key is used
Retries can produce duplicate ledger entries
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: unbounded workflow execution timeout
userStories.description: Start the workflow with no workflowExecutionTimeout or workflowRunTimeout so a stuck run lives forever.
acceptanceCriteria: Starter sets no workflow-level timeouts
Marked with a BAD IDEA comment

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: signal handler never registered
userStories.description: Define a cancelOrder signal with defineSignal, but never call setHandler for it, so signals sent to the workflow are never processed.
acceptanceCriteria: Signal is defined and documented but has no handler

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: saga with compensations that also fail
userStories.description: Add a compensation stack (refundCard, releaseInventory) that runs on failure, where the compensation activities themselves throw and have no retry or error handling.
acceptanceCriteria: Compensations can throw and are not guarded

userStories.title: BAD IDEA: code change that breaks replay
userStories.description: Add a documented v2 branch that inserts an extra activity call before chargeCard without using patched() or versioning, plus a script that demonstrates replaying an old history against it.
acceptanceCriteria: Unversioned change in command order is present
Replay demo script exists and is documented
